title: Orbit dimensions and boundaries for smooth connected algebraic groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field (every nonconstant polynomial in $k[t]$ has a root) [def-weil-field]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-av-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $G$ act on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Here affine means represented by $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An action is a morphism $a:G\times_kX\to X$ satisfying the unit and multiplication identities. For $x\in X(k)$ let $G_x$ be the closed subgroup scheme with $G_x(T)=\{g\in G(T):g x_T=x_T\}$, and let $O_x$ be the image of the orbit map $g\mapsto gx$, equipped with its reduced subscheme structure. Then $O_x$ is a smooth locally closed subscheme of $X$, the map $G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat, and $\dim O_x=\dim G-\dim G_x$. The closure $\overline{O_x}$ and its boundary $\overline{O_x}\setminus O_x$ are invariant; every orbit $O_y$ in that boundary satisfies $\dim O_y<\dim O_x$. Dimensions are those of [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. No reducedness of $X$ or of the stabilizers is required.

source.place: Milne, Algebraic Groups (2022 corrected text), Proposition 1.65 and Corollary 1.66 (orbit lemma), Propositions 7.4--7.6, printed pp.139--140 (smooth orbit, invariant closure and smaller-dimensional boundary), and Proposition 5.23, printed p.104 (quotient dimension), applied via Propositions 7.11--7.12. Local PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Write $q:G\to X$, $q(g)=gx$, and $S=q(|G|)$. The schemes $G,X$ are of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field is Noetherian). Any map between them with separated target is finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target]; affine coordinate maps are finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Thus Chevalley and generic flatness below have their finiteness hypotheses. Smoothness makes $G$ regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]; its identity makes it nonempty, so connectedness and [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] make $G$ integral. In particular $G$ is reduced and $Z=\overline S$ is irreducible. Every nonempty locally closed subset of a finite-type $k$-scheme contains a closed point by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], and these points are $k$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. We use these two statements to detect equality of locally closed subsets and to show that an open containing every closed point is the whole scheme. Reduced closed subschemes of these schemes are finite type since a closed immersion is proper, hence finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Their open subschemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], hence their open immersions are quasi-compact and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Composition preserves finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. This justifies the same finiteness assertions for $Z,O,B$ when constructed.

By [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image], $S$ is constructible. Choose an affine open $A$ meeting $Z$. The subset $S\cap A$ is nonempty and constructible in $A$; [lem-wf-affine-constructible-open](2) gives a nonempty relatively open subset $U$ of $Z\cap A$ contained in $S$. This is open in $Z$. For $g\in G(k)$, the map $t_g(z)=gz$ is an automorphism with inverse $t_{g^{-1}}$; equivariance $t_gq=qL_g$ gives $t_gS=S$ and $t_gZ=Z$. Put $V=\bigcup_{g\in G(k)}t_gU$. It is open in $Z$ and contained in $S$. Fix a closed $u\in U$. Every closed point of $G$ is $k$-rational, and the equality $q(h)=(hg_0^{-1})u$, where $q(g_0)=u$, shows that $q^{-1}(V)$ contains all of them. Here $g_0$ exists because the nonempty fibre over $u$ is finite type over $k$ by base change [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], so it has a closed $k$-point. Thus $q^{-1}(V)=G$ by the closed-point detection in step 1, and $S=V$. This proves local closedness, without identifying the scheme's whole point set with its closed points.

source.place: Proposition 1.65(b), p.27; Appendix A.15; Stacks 054J and 0478.

proof.text: Give $Z$ its reduced closed structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and give the open $S\subset Z$ its induced structure $O$. Since $G$ is reduced, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factors $q$ through $Z$; its image lies in the open $O$, giving $q:G\to O$. This map is surjective by the definition of $S$. Its image is irreducible, so the nonempty reduced $O$ is integral. Each $t_g$ restricts to an automorphism of $O$: reduced closed structures are unique, and open restriction preserves them. The locally closed subscheme $O$ of the separated $X$ is separated (its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $X$). Thus $q:G\to O$ is finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target]. Choose a nonempty open $W\subset O$ on which $q$ is flat by [lem-sbc-generic-flatness]. The translates $t_gW$ cover $O$: choose $w\in W(k)$ and lifts $g_w,g_y\in G(k)$ of $w$ and each $y\in O(k)$, as in step 2; then $y=t_{g_yg_w^{-1}}w$. The union is open and contains every closed point, so step 1 makes it all of $O$. In the square $qL_g=t_gq$, both horizontal maps are isomorphisms. On stalks the maps for $q$ over $t_gW$ are therefore isomorphic to the flat stalk maps over $W$. Hence $q$ is flat everywhere and, being surjective, faithfully flat. This uses only flatness, not smoothness of $q$.

source.place: Proposition 1.65(a),(c), p.27; Proposition 7.4(b), pp.139--140; Stacks 01J3 and 052A.

proof.text: An algebraically closed field is perfect: in positive characteristic every $a$ has a root of $T^p-a$. Thus the reduced finite-type $O$ is geometrically reduced by [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect]. Its smooth locus is a dense open by [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open]. Every $t_g$ is a $k$-isomorphism, so it preserves this locus. A nonempty smooth open has a closed $k$-point; transitivity carries it to every closed point of $O$. Its complement is closed and has no closed points, so is empty by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space]. Consequently $O$ is smooth over $k$.

The identity stalk of $G$ has finite dimension by [lem-kun-finite-type-local-dimension], so [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] makes $\dim G$ finite. Applied to the original composite $G\to O\hookrightarrow X$, whose image closure in $X$ is $Z$, [lem-zl-irreducible-fibre-dimension-lower-bound] gives $\dim G=\dim Z+r$ with $r\in\mathbb N$. Thus $\dim Z$ is finite. Its dense open $O$ has the same dimension by [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison] and subspace monotonicity. The fibre $q^{-1}(x)$ is $G_x$: on each test scheme $T$ its points are exactly the $g\in G(T)$ with $gx_T=x_T$. The action identities restrict multiplication, inverse and identity to it. The section $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ of a separated morphism is a closed immersion (base change of the diagonal); its pullback makes $G_x$ a closed finite-type subgroup of $G$, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Now [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point] applied to $G\xrightarrow q O\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $e\mapsto x$ gives $\dim_eG=\dim_eG_x+\dim_xO$, since $q$ is flat. For $G,G_x$, [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] and [lem-ag-rational-point-stalk-topological-local-dimension] identify these identity local dimensions with their global dimensions, without reducedness assumptions. The irreducible $O$ has its unique component of finite dimension; [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] gives $\dim_xO=\dim O$. Consequently $\dim G=\dim G_x+\dim O$, equivalently $\dim O=\dim G-\dim G_x$.

source.place: Proposition 5.23, p.104; Appendix A.72; stabilizer definition, p.140; Stacks 02JS, 0A21, 00OU and 00P1.

proof.text: Put $B=(Z\setminus O)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Each $t_g$ preserves $O$, its closure $Z$, and its complement $B$ as sets. This gives scheme invariance as follows. For $T=Z$ or $B$, [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] and [lem-pc-smooth-flat] make $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ flat with geometrically reduced fibres. Hence $G\times_kT$ is reduced by [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback]. This product is finite type over $k$ by base change and composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Its closed points are $k$-rational, and their images under the action lie in $T$, by the preceding set invariance. Density of closed points implies that the whole action image is contained in the closed subset underlying $T$. The reduced-source factorization theorem [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] now factors $G\times_kT\to X$ through the reduced closed subscheme $T\subset X$. The restricted multiplication and identity laws follow by composing with the immersion into $X$. This proves invariance even as reduced subschemes, despite possible nilpotents in $X$.

source.place: Proposition 7.5(a),(b), p.140; Appendix A.43; Stacks 056T and 01J3.

proof.text: The dense open $O\subset Z$ has $\dim Z=\dim O$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison] and subspace monotonicity. This is finite by step 5. Since $Z$ is irreducible and $B$ is a proper closed subset, any strict chain of irreducible closed subsets in $B$ can be extended by appending $Z$. Thus, if $B$ is nonempty, $\dim B+1\le\dim Z$. If $B$ is empty there are no boundary orbits. For $y\in B(k)$, invariance factors the orbit map through $B$, so its image $O_y$ is contained in $B$ and $\dim O_y\le\dim B<\dim O$. To see the subspace inequality directly, close each irreducible closed set of a chain in the ambient space; intersecting back with the subspace recovers the original chain, so strict inclusions remain strict. All constructions and arguments applied to $x$ apply to any such $y$, establishing the asserted boundary orbit statement.

source.place: Orbit lemma 1.66, pp.27--28; Proposition 7.6, p.140; Stacks 0A21; elementary chain argument.

Context: no new nodes; statement and stmt_deps unchanged; item still unsplit with an empty proof on clones/live and clones/side-live; no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply. This is the third delivery after L's promotion return. Against the 76896175 snapshot, only step 3 and the split_report summary changed. Step 3 now proves O is separated (as a locally closed subscheme of the separated X), cites Nagata (b) for G->O being of finite type, and writes out the translate cover y = t_{g_y g_w^{-1}} w; all of this is correct. Source: the local Milne iAG2017 (pdftotext), Prop 1.65(a)-(c), the orbit lemma 1.66, Prop 7.4(b) and 7.5, and the isotropy definition on p.140. The steps follow this route; Prop 5.23 is replaced by flat fibre-dimension additivity at e, which is valid. No SGA is cited. Step checks: (1) Noetherian, finite type to a separated target, regular+connected+nonempty gives integral, Jacobson closed points are rational. (2) Chevalley plus lem-wf-affine-constructible-open(2) on an affine A; S is irreducible so the closure of S∩A is Z∩A; q^{-1}(V) contains all closed points, so S=V. (3) O is integral, generic flatness hypotheses hold, translates cover O, faithful flatness follows without smoothness of q. (4) k perfect gives geometrically reduced, a dense smooth locus, then homogeneity. (5) dim G is finite via the identity stalk; the zl lower bound makes dim Z finite; the fibre of G->O over x is G_x (monomorphism); flat additivity at e; identity-dimension needs no reducedness of G_x; def-kun-dimension's dim_x is the same as topological-dimension-at-point. (6) G×T is reduced (smooth implies flat with geometrically reduced fibres, flat-reduced pullback) before the factorization is applied. (7) Appending Z to chains in B gives the strict drop; the empty boundary is handled. Edge cases: fixed point; G_m on A^1; SL2 on A^2 (2=3-1); char p with x+a^p (G_x=α_p, q flat but not smooth); nonreduced X. I accept the 11 generic tool_uses. Maintainer note: Q15 lem-sfb-git-orbit-closure-dimension overlaps with this item and could cite it; it was not created by this delivery.
